{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (HDI / Company Internet Site Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review findings and proposed redlines

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The commercial spine of the deal is acceptable: the fee construct is purely revenue-share with no minimum commitment, there is no MFN and no non-solicit burdening us, governing law is New York (our preferred law), the non-compete in Section 6.1 sits at our fallback, and HDI's reciprocal two-year restraint in Section 6.3 runs in our favour.

The substantive problem is what the Agreement omits. There is **no limitation of liability, no indemnity, no insurance requirement, no IP ownership or assignment provision, no performance warranty, and no transition assistance or data-return obligation**. HDI designs, develops and hosts the Site and, per Section 8.1, holds our Content, user information and data — yet nothing allocates ownership of the Site or the customer data, nothing obliges HDI to defend an IP infringement claim, and nothing requires HDI to carry coverage or to hand our data back on exit. Both parties are exposed to unlimited liability.

The two Company-adverse economic terms are the Section 4.2 Termination Payment (one half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, uncapped, triggered even by ordinary 90-day non-renewal) and the open-ended Section 6.1 exclusivity tied to an indefinitely auto-renewing term. Together they mean we have no genuinely penalty-free exit. We have also proposed narrow fixes to the unlimited record-inspection right (Section 3.4), the 90-day non-renewal window (Section 4.1), and the licence grant in Section 1.4, which names only "the Company" and excludes affiliates and contractors.

Eight items are compliant or benefit us and are not redlined.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant (at fallback) | § 6.1 (with § 6.2 carve-out; § 6.3 restrains HDI) | Term-only restraint, product/channel limited, closeout carve-out. No internal-development or acquisition carve-out — noted, not redlined. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 10.5 | New York law (preferred). No arbitration or foreign/exclusive venue anywhere; absence of express New York County venue noted only. |
| Medium | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Missing** | § 9 (insertion as § 9(c)); survival via § 10.7 | No cap, no consequential-damages waiver — unlimited exposure both ways. Inserted mutual cap (greater of 12 months' fees / USD 1m), waiver and uncapped Excluded Claims, with Company payment obligations (incl. Termination Payment) excluded. **Insertion failed verification — requires manual placement.** |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | § 1.8 (runs in our favour); §§ 3, 6, 7, 10 | No MFN burdens us; HDI must promote the Site no less favourably than its own catalog titles. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 3.1; § 4.1 | 30% of Net Sales above an $11,000 monthly floor; no minimum, shortfall or take-or-pay. Termination Payment and exclusivity addressed under separate rules. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 5.4; § 6 | No solicit/no-hire covenant on us; § 5.4 is a General Manager liaison provision only. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | New § 4.3 (after § 4.2) | § 1.4 access is term-only; § 8 has no return duty; § 10.7 survival omits exit mechanics. Inserted six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable data return, certified deletion. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | **Deviation** | § 9 (insertion as § 9(c)) | § 9 covers corporate reps only; no warranty of the design, development, hosting or maintenance services, and no remedy. Inserted 90-day conformance warranty with repair/replace/re-perform/refund. No "AS IS" disclaimer present. |
| Low | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 10.3 | Bare successors-and-assigns clause: HDI may assign this hosting engagement freely, including to a competitor. Proposed Company affiliate/successor freedom, reasonableness-qualified consent gate plus competitor bar on HDI, and no HDI right on our change of control. |
| Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 3.4 (records protected by § 8.3) | Notice, timing and cost all meet or exceed preferred, but frequency is unlimited. Proposed a once-per-twelve-month cap. |
| Low | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 6.1 (with §§ 4.1, 4.2(a), 1.6) | Exclusivity runs for an indefinitely auto-renewing term; only performance exit is the narrow 70-day launch failure right. Proposed fallback: 12-month cap with automatic release on HDI service level or delivery failure. § 6.3 left intact. |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | New § 9(c) | No indemnity, defence or hold-harmless in either direction; no IP infringement cover for the Site HDI builds and hosts. Inserted HDI-side indemnity (third-party IP, breach of law, HDI-caused data disclosure, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice/control/cooperation and a carve-out for Company Content and Marks. No Company indemnity added. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | New § 10.9 (General Provisions, § 10) | No insurance requirement despite HDI's access to Content, user information and data (§ 8.1). Inserted CGL 1m/2m, E&O 2m, cyber 5m, workers' comp, certificates on request; fallback (E&O 1m / cyber 2m) offered in comment. |
| Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Missing** | New § 5.5 (cf. §§ 1.1–1.3, 2.1, 2.2, 6.1, 7.1, 8) | No ownership or assignment provision: nothing states who owns the Site, work product or customer/transaction data. Inserted Company ownership and HDI assignment of deliverables, Company retention of Company Data, HDI pre-existing IP retained with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to us, and no joint ownership. |
| Low | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 4.2 (cf. §§ 3.1, 4.1, 1.6) | Uncapped stipulated payment (50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000) triggered even by ordinary non-renewal; can exceed a full year's fees. Proposed fallback three-month cap as the sole amount due; § 4.2(c) instalments unobjectionable once capped. |
| Low | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 1.4 (cf. §§ 6.1, 10.3, 4) | Sole inbound grant names only "the Company" — no affiliates or contractors and no path to add them. Proposed one appended sentence extending to affiliates and contractors, confirming successor exercise and irrevocability absent termination under § 4. |
| Low | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Deviation** | § 4.1 | One-year renewals are acceptable, but the 90-day non-renewal window exceeds the 60-day fallback ceiling. Proposed 30-day window (60-day fallback offered), plus a renewal reminder and uplift cap. No uplift language currently appears. |
| Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 4.1 / § 4.2 | 90-day mutual convenience right sits at fallback and is not redlined; the failure is the uncapped § 4.2 Termination Payment, which denies us a penalty-free exit. Capped at three months' fees. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **No vendor indemnity (INDEMN, missing).** HDI gives no IP infringement defence for a Site it builds and hosts. This fails even the fallback and is walk-away territory; nothing in § 7.2 or the confidentiality provisions supplies an indemnity.
2. **No insurance (INSURANCE, missing).** Total absence of coverage for a vendor processing personal data is walk-away territory.
3. **Unlimited inspection frequency (AUDIT, § 3.4, deviation).** Unlimited audits fail the fallback and sit in walk-away territory; cured by a single once-per-year sentence.

Close to the line, and to be resolved in the same pass:

- **§ 4.2 Termination Payment (LD / T4C).** An uncapped penalty triggered by routine termination approaches walk-away territory. Our preference is deletion; we have proposed the three-month fallback cap.
- **§ 6.1 exclusivity (EXCLUSIVITY).** Open-ended exclusivity with no performance-based release approaches walk-away territory.
- **§ 1.4 licence scope (LICENSE).** Affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them approaches the walk-away description.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Fix the LOL insertion.** The mutual limitation of liability inserted at § 9(c) failed verification. Place it manually and confirm it is picked up by the § 10.7 survival provision and that Company payment obligations, including the Termination Payment, are excluded from the cap.
2. **Confirm the repaired insertions read correctly in context** — new § 4.3 (transition and data return), § 9(c) (warranty and indemnity), § 5.5 (IP ownership), § 10.9 (insurance) — and check numbering against the executed exhibit.
3. **Open negotiation on the three walk-away items first** (indemnity, insurance, audit frequency). The audit fix is a one-line cap and should be conceded readily; indemnity and insurance are standard vendor terms and we should not sign without them.
4. **Negotiate the exit economics as a package**: cap the § 4.2 Termination Payment at three months' fees, cap § 6.1 exclusivity at twelve months with automatic release on HDI service level or delivery failure, and shorten the § 4.1 non-renewal window to 30 days (60-day fallback available). We are leaving HDI's reciprocal § 6.3 restraint intact and should say so when trading.
5. **Hold the minor points in reserve.** If HDI reopens the document for its own reasons, we would add express New York County venue (§ 10.5), the § 6.1 internal-development and acquisition carve-outs, an independent auditor under § 3.4, and a renewal price-uplift cap. None of these justify a redline on their own.
6. **Business input required** on the § 4.2 exposure: please confirm projected Net Sales so we can quantify the uncapped Termination Payment against three months' fees before the next call."}
